title: Acrolein + PFA Perfusion for Immunocytochemistry
author: Cleyde V Helena
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tb9eir6

steps.title: Prepare animal for perfusion
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the animal with Nembutal, open the chest cavity, inject 0.1 cc heparin into the heart apex, clamp the descending aorta to eliminate whole‑body perfusion, and cut the atrium.

substeps.instruction: Inject 0.1 cc heparin into heart apex

steps.title: First saline‑nitrite rinse
steps.instruction: Perfuse 0.9 % saline containing sodium nitrite (concentration not specified) until the effluent is clear, using about 150–200 ml for a 225–250 g rat.

steps.title: Acrolein/PFA fixation perfusion
steps.instruction: Prepare a fixative of 8 % paraformaldehyde in 0.5 M monobasic potassium phosphate and 0.5 M dibasic potassium phosphate made up with distilled water; add acrolein just before perfusion. Perfuse this solution until the animal becomes hard (front feet stiff), using approximately 150–200 ml for a 225–250 g rat. If using a sealed bottle or flask, slowly release pressure before perfusing.

steps.title: Second saline‑nitrite rinse
steps.instruction: Perfuse about 150 ml of the same 0.9 % saline‑sodium nitrite solution. No post‑fixation step is required.
